sections.heading: Hold for evidence, then promote
text: Fictional, editable explanation. Versions, samples, p95 values, timings and policy outcomes are authored; this is not live telemetry, a statistical proof or an executable rollout policy. The source chip is a pattern reference, not evidence for these numbers.
bullets: Example promotion requires at least 1000 v2 requests in one named completed window, failed-request rate at most 1%, and p95 at most 250 ms. These are illustrative thresholds, not production recommendations.
Configured traffic weights sum to 100. They are router settings, not observed request fractions or pod-count percentages. Cohort names stay fixed to track v1 and v2.

Error rate uses failed requests / all requests from the same window. p95 is a separately authored distribution statistic; it cannot be derived from those counts. Readiness, routing and sampled health are separate.

Only v2 is sampled in these windows; the old cohort tile is an explicitly older baseline report. This is not a matched-control comparison. Deployment capacity and data compatibility are assumptions of this example.

steps.text: Both versions are deployed and ready. New v2 has zero configured traffic and no sampled request health. A ready process is not a passing canary.

sample.detail: 0 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

decision.detail: HOLD: expose a bounded canary before evaluating it

steps.text: The router acknowledges a 95/5 weight configuration. W1 starts for v2; zero completed requests means no error-rate denominator, not a 0% failure rate.

sample.detail: 0 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

decision.detail: HOLD at 5%: collect the named window

steps.text: W1 closes with 200 requests and one failure. Its error and latency values fit the example ceilings, but 200 is below the 1000-request minimum. Hold the traffic configuration.

sample.detail: 200 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

decision.detail: HOLD at 5%: insufficient sample despite values within limits

steps.text: Separate, non-overlapping W2 closes with 1000 requests and five failures. All authored gates pass. Authorize 50%, while the acknowledged routing configuration remains 5% until the next step.

sample.detail: 1000 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

decision.detail: PROMOTE TO 50% authorized from W2; not yet applied

steps.text: The router acknowledges 50/50. W3 is a new window: its measurements and gates start empty rather than carrying a previous passing value into a different traffic configuration.

sample.detail: 0 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

steps.text: W3 closes with 1000 requests and four failures. The example policy authorizes 100% after the checks pass; routing is still 50% at this decision beat.

sample.detail: 1000 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

decision.detail: PROMOTE TO 100% authorized from W3; not yet applied

steps.text: The router acknowledges 0/100. The old v1 deployment still exists at zero configured traffic. New W4 health is unknown; continued monitoring is required and its outcome is outside this story.

sample.detail: 0 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

decision.detail: 100% configuration APPLIED; W4 monitoring remains pending

sections.heading: Abort the canary and restore routing
text: Fictional, editable explanation. Versions, samples, p95 values, timings and policy outcomes are authored; this is not live telemetry, a statistical proof or an executable rollout policy. The source chip is a pattern reference, not evidence for these numbers.
bullets: Example promotion requires at least 1000 v2 requests in one named completed window, failed-request rate at most 1%, and p95 at most 250 ms. These are illustrative thresholds, not production recommendations.
Configured traffic weights sum to 100. They are router settings, not observed request fractions or pod-count percentages. Cohort names stay fixed to track v1 and v2.

Error rate uses failed requests / all requests from the same window. p95 is a separately authored distribution statistic; it cannot be derived from those counts. Readiness, routing and sampled health are separate.

Only v2 is sampled in these windows; the old cohort tile is an explicitly older baseline report. This is not a matched-control comparison. Deployment capacity and data compatibility are assumptions of this example.

steps.text: An independent rollout begins with both versions ready and v2 receiving zero configured traffic. Baseline readiness does not prove the new request path is healthy.

sample.detail: 0 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

steps.text: The router acknowledges a 95/5 configuration and opens W1 for v2.

sample.detail: 0 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

steps.text: W1 closes with 1000 requests, 25 failures and p95 310 ms. Both ceilings fail. The policy orders a traffic rollback; the previous 5% configuration is still acknowledged at this beat.

sample.detail: 1000 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

decision.detail: ROLL BACK TRAFFIC authorized: W1 failed both ceilings

steps.text: The router acknowledges 100/0. The failing W1 evidence stays visible with its original 5% window weight. New v2 remains deployed; this traffic rollback does not reverse writes, schema changes, or already in-flight work.

sample.detail: 1000 / 1000 minimum requests in the named canary window

decision.detail: Traffic rollback APPLIED; retain W1 for investigation

sections.heading: Trial boot, confirmation and a held wave
text: Fictional ten-device campaign. All versions, package checks, health outcomes and reports are authored. This models a two-slot bootloader configured for reversible test upgrades, with a valid retained image and a policy permitting reversion. It does not promise that every bootloader or device can roll back.
bullets: The version table records the latest available reports, not a continuously known device state. Running image, persistent confirmation and the other-slot image are separate facts.
A and B are individual canaries. The eight-device later wave is an explicitly homogeneous last-reported v1 cohort and never receives v2 authorization in this story.
Signature and hardware compatibility checks do not establish runtime health. Missing telemetry does not establish confirmation, failure or rollback.
A successful v1 self-test after reversion is different from passing the v2 release gate. A confirmed v2 image does not automatically revert with an unconfirmed peer.

steps.text: Two canaries and the later wave last reported confirmed v1. Target v2 is only a campaign intent. No package has been accepted or written yet.

cells.value: HOLD · all 8 remain outside v2 rollout

compat.detail: Compatibility and rollback policy not checked

steps.text: The example package passes signature, board compatibility and rollback-policy checks. Active and confirmed versions are still v1. A valid image is not proof of runtime health.

cells.value: HOLD · all 8 remain outside v2 rollout

compat.detail: Authored board compatibility / rollback policy check

steps.text: Both canaries report v2 fully written to their inactive slot. They still run confirmed v1. The later wave has no candidate image and receives no update command.

steps.text: Both canaries report trial boots of v2, not yet confirmed; v1 is retained in the other slot. Self-test results have not arrived. Running v2 alone does not admit the next wave.

steps.text: Canary A reports self-test success and persistent confirmation of v2. B sends no fresh report. B may have changed locally: its last trial report does not establish its current confirmation or running image.

compat.detail: Authored board compatibility / rollback policy check

a.detail: Fresh v2 self-test and confirmation report

b.detail: Missing fresh report; do not infer rollback or success

steps.text: B reconnects with a fresh boot report: its unconfirmed trial reverted to v1 on reset and v1 self-test passed. A remains confirmed on v2. Stop expansion; a rollback of A would need a separately authorized update compatible with the device policy.
